title: Classic Sixth Edition: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "When you have been bitten with fangs of granite, you start to long for the ivory sabers of tigers." —Norin the Wary
"My mother once told me angels sing their swords' names with each strike." —Sisay, Captain of the *Weatherlight*
Some fight for honor and some for gold, but the militia fight for hearth and home.
Asked how it survived a run-in with a bog imp, the pegasus just shook its mane and burped.
"Hang out our banners on the outward walls; / The cry is still, 'They come'; our castle's strength / Will laugh a siege to scorn." —William Shakespeare, *Macbeth*
"And the flamingos said, 'Get out of our nest—we can't be seen with the likes of you!' So, the griffin ate them." —Azeworai, "The Ugly Bird"
Avenant's archers are also trained as poets, so that each arrow is guided by a fragment of verse.
Glory surged through her and radiance surrounded her. All things were possible with the blessing of the Divine.
"My goat was a small price to pay for the chance to see the hunting griffin dive and seize it." —Suq'Ata trader
"I do not teach. I simply reveal." —Daudi, Femeref tutor
"If I have learned anything as a wizard it is this: never fight your own battles." —Waffa, sorcerer of Nyomba
"Archers, ballistae—you can't even get near the island of Avenant." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
"Destiny, chance, fate, fortune—they're all just ways of claiming your successes without claiming your failures." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
Icatia's once-peaceful towns faced increasing attacks from orcs and goblins as the climate cooled. By the time the empire fell, they were little more than armed camps.
"The true dishonor for a soldier is surviving the war." —Telim'Tor
"Make people wait for what they want, and you have power over them. This is as true for merchants and militia as it is for cooks and couples." —Gwendlyn Di Corci
Honorable in battle, generous in death. —Motto of the Kjeldoran Royal Guard
"I do not miss sunlight. The very memory of it burns my eyes." —Volrath
"If it bears wings, I will pin it to the skies over Tefemburu." —Roya, Zhalfirin archer
"The faith of Serra is borne on wings of hope." —Gulsen, abbey matron
A blazing light to drive out the shadows.
For the first time in his life, Grakk felt a little warm and fuzzy inside.
"They knew Bantau was lost when, to hide the pearl he had found on the beach, he swallowed it—and soon grew wings." —Hakim, Loreweaver
Unicorns don't care if you believe in them any more than you care if they believe in you.
"These things will protect you while I'm gone, remind you of my love for you." —"Love Song of Night and Day"
"The meek shall fight as one, and they shall overcome even the greatest of foes." —Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
"My soldiers fought without hesitation, died without doubt." —Sidar Jabari
Healers ultimately acquire the divine gifts of spiritual and physical wholeness. The most devout are also granted the ability to pass physical wholeness on to others.
"Just think of me as the storm before the calm." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
"I have seen your strength imbued in angels' wings, and I have felt your sorrow rain down on the ruins brought by the Lord of the Wastes." —Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator
The less you have, the harder you fight for it.
"Hold your position! Leave doubt for the dying!" —Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*
"There is no sweeter music than the wails of a dying dragon." —Rashida Scalebane
I heard their eerie howling, the wolves calling their kindred across the frozen plains.
The griffin's shadow gives courage to the righteous and dread to the idle.
His presence brings not only a strong arm but also renewed hope.
Sharper than wind, lighter than air.
"Flame grows gentle with but a little distance." —Orim, Samite healer
As insubstantial, and as powerful, as the wind that carries it.
A lie always returns; be careful how you catch it.
"Once great literature—now great litter." —Jaya Ballard, task mage
"Temper, temper." —Ertai, wizard adept
In front of every great wizard is a doomed apprentice.
Up and down, over and through, back around— the joke's on you.
First the insult, then the injury.
Dreams' riches are easily spent. —Suq'Ata adage
"I've seen fog so thick you could cut it, but none that could cut me." —Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*
"Huge walls of ice block further travel. We can't believe they are natural." —Disa the Restless, journal entry
"One moment I was walking along the beach, and the next I was high in the air, staring into a hideous smiling face." —Tarub, Suq'Ata sailor
"So like men are they: a hardened shell with fragile flesh beneath." —Selenia, dark angel
"We can fight with you or against you. After my day, I'd prefer the former." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
"Madness and genius are separated only by degrees of success." —Sidar Jabari
A master of tactics, the lord of Atlantis makes his people bold in battle merely by arriving to lead them.
"Um . . . oh . . . what was I saying?" —Reveka, wizard savant
Are merfolk humans with fins, or are humans merfolk with feet?
"To the tutors, a 'poem of sand' was of little account, a 'poem of ivory,' priceless." —Afari, *Tales*
The phantom warrior comes from nowhere and returns there just as quickly.
"Ahh! Opposable digits!"
Occasionally members of the Institute of Arcane Study acquire a taste for worldly pleasures. Seldom do they have trouble finding employment.
"Wealth is a good thing, compared to poverty—your food is better, your robes are softer, and your companions have bathed more recently." —Kukemssa pirate
"The memory of your existence will fade like the final stars of morning." —Kaervek
"Barrin taught me that the hardest lessons to grasp are the ones you've already learned." —Ertai, wizard adept
Nethya stiffened suddenly, head cocked as if straining to hear some distant sound, then fell lifeless to the ground.
The owl asks but never answers.
Water is life. Or perhaps it is just something to wash it down with.
"Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook or run a line round his tongue?" —*The Bible*, Job 41:1
She had expected death to roar, to thunder, to growl. She did not recognize it when it came hissing to her side.
"To hide the truth is more than folly—it is fatal." —Sorine Relicbane, Soldevi heretic
Call it the thinking mage's version of brute force.
Storm crow descending, winter unending. Storm crow departing, summer is starting.
"It is nature that gives us our boundaries and nature that enforces them." —Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
"Vodalian rank is displayed by the colors and patterns of their skin. Beware the color red; that is the badge of the empress's favor." —Corbio, pearl diver
When no falcons fly, beware the sky. —Femeref aphorism
"No bird soars too high, if he soars with his own wings." —William Blake, *The Marriage of Heaven and Hell*
" . . . When the trees bow down their heads, The wind is passing by." —Christina Rossetti, "Who Has Seen the Wind?"
Some smiles show cheer; some merely show teeth.
"An innocent man died because of my anger. That knowledge will haunt me for all eternity." —Karn, silver golem
"What you call decay, I call ripening. You'll gain no sustenance from this harvest." —Kaervek
"You are wrong," Volrath said. "I do not hate the living. They often prove quite useful to me." And then he laughed.
Don't be fooled by their looks. Think of them as little knives with wings.
Their stench was vile and strong enough, but not nearly as powerful as their hunger.
It moved through the troops leaving no footprints, save on their souls.
A rhino's bargain —Femeref expression meaning "a situation with no choices"
"Strength it has, but at the cost of a continuous supply of energy. Such failure can bear only one result." —Execution order of Endrek Sahr, master breeder
"These moonless, foreign skies keep me in thrall. Dark whispers echo in the night, and I cannot resist." —Selenia, dark angel
"The dead make good soldiers. They can't disobey orders, they never surrender, and they don't stop fighting when a random body part falls off." —Nevinyrral, *Necromancer's Handbook*
"Wherever water is lacking, all things suffer." —Autumn Willow
"If it is weak, either kill it or ignore it. Anything else honors it." —Kaervek
The highway of fear is the shortest route to defeat.
"Angels are simply extensions of truth upon the fabric of life—and there is far more dark than light." —Baron Sengir
"What is crueler? To let a wound of the heart fester, or to simply cut it out?" —Crovax
"Could there be a fouler act? No doubt the baron knows of one." —Autumn Willow
Not all shadows are cast by light—some are cast by darkness.
A full coffin is like a full coffer—both are attractive to thieves.
"There is no calamity greater than lavish desires. There is no greater guilt than discontentment. And there is no greater disaster than greed." —Lao Tsu, *Tao Te Ching*, (trans. Chan)
"But I signed nothing!" —Taraneh, Suq'Ata mage
"They shall drink sorrow's dregs. They shall kill those whom once they loved." —Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer
"Bind me to thee, my soul to thine. I am your servant and your slave. Blood for blood, flesh for flesh, Leshrac, my lord." —Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer
Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—but those who go with her are never the same.
The hardest of wizards can have the softest of minds.
"The past is a ghost that haunts you from the moment it exists until the moment you don't." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
As the poisoned land spreads, so does the nightmare's rage and terrifying strength.
"It is terrible how one brief action can live forever in memory." —Jolrael
"There will come a time when the voices of soil and seedling will sing only laments." —Oracle *en*-Vec
"How can you claim the gods are merciless when they robbed the snake of its limbs to give the other creatures a sporting chance?" —Hakim, Loreweaver
"Aw, he's just a silly, dirty little man. What's to be afraid of?"
The earth cannot hold that which magic commands.
"Men and rats both hunger: we for our playthings; they, for us." —Crovax

"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose, Nor spake, nor moved their eyes; It had been strange, even in a dream, To have seen those dead men rise." —Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
"I have seen the night torn into thin darkling strips and woven into shapes too bleak for dreams." —Crovax
When the alliance between Balduvia and Kjeldor deprived Stromgald of easy victories, its agents were forced to fuel their rituals with their own flesh.
There are medicines for all afflictions but idleness. —Suq'Ata saying
"I write upon clean white parchment with a sharp quill and the blood of my students, divining their secrets." —Shauku, Endbringer
He controlled the zombies even before his own death; now nothing can make them betray him.
"You can't get there from here. Well, you can—it just won't be fun." —Ertai, wizard adept
"Not all minotaurs are tribal. Some are freelance." —Eron the Relentless
"The shamans? Ha! They are craven cows not capable of true magic." —Irini Sengir

"Barbarian raids were a concern to those living in the northwest provinces, but the skyknights never dealt with the problem in a systematic way. They thought of the Balduvians as an 'amusing model' of their forebears' culture." —*Kjeldor: Ice Civilization*
Fire never dies alone.
"The fishers will throw out their nets and draw them back filled with dust." —Oracle *en*-Vec
"Why do we trade with those despicable elves? You don't live in forests, you burn them!" —Avram Garrisson, Leader of the Knights of Stromgald
"Dragonfire forged me a warrior." —Rashida Scalebane
"If your blood doesn't run hot, I will make it run in the sands!" —Maraxus of Keld
Want all, lose all. —Zhalfirin aphorism

Fire elementals are ruthless infernos, annihilating and consuming their foes in a frenzied holocaust. Crackling and blazing, they sear swift, terrible paths, leaving the land charred and scorched in their wake.
"Magic's only part of it, my friend. Diet does the rest." —Suq'Ata trader
"Anger is fleeting; remorse is eternal." —Karn, silver golem
"The spirit of the flame is the spirit of change." —Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain
"O! it is excellent / To have a giant's strength, but it is tyrannous / To use it like a giant." —William Shakespeare, *Measure for Measure*
"From down here we can make the whole wall collapse!" "Uh, yeah, boss, but how do we get out?"
They talk a good fight.
"When you're a goblin, you don't have to step forward to be a hero—everyone else just has to step back!" —Biggum Flodrot, goblin veteran
To be king, Numsgil did in Blog, who did in Unkful, who did in Viddle, who did in Loll, who did in Alrok . . . .
"Next!"
"Goblins bred underground, their numbers hidden from the enemy until it was too late." —*Sarpadian Empires*, vol. IV
Anyone can get around a cyclops, but few can stand in its way.
"Some have said there is no subtlety to destruction. You know what? They're dead." —Jaya Ballard, task mage
"The raging waters had swept away trees, bridges, and even houses. My healers had much work to do." —Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
"Those who fear the darkness have never seen what the light can do." —Selenia, dark angel
Only the heroic and the mad follow mountain goat trails.
In a rare display of ingenuity, the orcs invented an incredibly destructive weapon. Most orcish artillerists are those who dared criticize its effectiveness.
"Hi!ni!ya! Behold the man of flint, that's me! / Four lightnings zigzag from me, strike and return." —Navajo war chant
He raged at the world, at his family, at his life. But mostly he just raged.
Many mages have been consumed by their work.
"Flog and Squee / Up the tree / See the army / Flee, flee, flee." —Goblin nursery rhyme/war cry
"I fear anything with teeth measured in handspans!" —Norin the Wary
Chains of leaping fire and sizzling lightning laid waste the artificers' handiwork, sparing not a single device.
Lightning tethers souls to the world. —Kor saying
It prefers its meals cooked.
"There are times solid ground gives precious little comfort." —Talibah, embermage
Don't insult a Talruum unless your mount is swift. —Suq'Ata saying
"Where do you run when the earth becomes your enemy?" —Naimag, Femeref philosopher
"I saw the wizard gesturing, but I didn't guess his plan until my aesthir cried out and went into a dive." —Arna Kennerüd, skyknight
"When traveling the Great Desert avoid wearing the scales of lizards, for the Viashino rule the sands and look poorly on the skinning of their cousins." —*Zhalfirin Guide to the Desert*
Speed and fire are always a deadly combination.
My thunder comes before the lightning; my lightning comes before the clouds; my rain dries all the land it touches. What am I? —Femeref riddle
"Struggle, and you will only fan the flames." —Talibah, embermage
Thinking of dinner made Squee realize that the forest was probably thinking the same thing.
These stealthy felines have survived so many battles that some believe they must possess many lives.
"Mold could catch you." —Suq'Ata insult
"Big plants not only good for hidin', but full o' tasty bugs, too." —Squee, goblin cabin hand
"Tonight we'll eat a farewell feast. Cold corn porridge is not enough. / Let's peel papayas, pineapples, and mangoes, drink coconut milk, / and bake bananas." —"Love Song of Night and Day"
"Did clouds dance in his eyes, did thorns play at his fingertips?" —Shesul Fass, faerie bard
Elves know where to harvest the best of the forest, for they planted it there themselves.
Sometimes it is better to be swift of foot than strong of swordarm. —Elven proverb
"I tell you, there was so many arrows flying about you couldn't hardly see the sun. So I says to young Angus, 'Well, at least now we're fighting in the shade!'"
". . . and when the farmer awoke the next morning, all the seeds from his field were once again in their sacks." —Afari, *Tales*
"I'd rather fight on foreign soil. That way, if I lose I can blame it on the terrain." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
"They say a Zhalfirin archer can split the eye of a griffin. Nonsense, of course; they have no faith to guide their darts." —Nuru, Femeref archer
"I've been insulted by drunks in a hundred inns, but never as skillfully or annoyingly as by those blasted brownies." —General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox
"Do we know what we're doing? Yes—the will of Freyalise." —Laina of the Elvish Council
It's not far into the trap, as the crow flies.
"In the soil of leadership sprout the seeds of immortality." —Kaysa, Elder Druid of the Juniper

Don't try to outrun one of Dominaria's grizzlies; it'll catch you, knock you down, and eat you. Of course, you could run up a tree. In that case you'll get a nice view before it knocks the tree down and eats you.
One bone broken for every twig snapped underfoot. —Llanowar penalty for trespassing
When setting a snare, success depends not on the quality of the trap, but the quality of the bait.
No two see the same Maro.
Spring follows winter —Elvish expression meaning "all things pass"
The dogs of war are nothing compared to the cats.
"A mysterious people indeed. Their origins are as secret as their traditions." —Lord Magnus of Llanowar
Rath forces plants from its surface as one presses whey from cheese.
The soldiers chopped and chopped, and still the great tree stood, frowning down at them.
"But no one heard the snake's gentle hiss for peace over the elephant's trumpeting of war." —Afari, *Tales*
"I've dreamt of a second harvest but fear I will not see it." —Asmira, holy avenger

"Flourishing during the Ice Age, these wurms were the bane of all Kjeldorans. Their great size and ferocity made them the subject of countless nightmares—they embodied the worst of the Ice Age." —*Kjeldor: Ice Civilization*
Moving without sound, swift figures pass through branches and undergrowth completely unhindered. One with the trees around them, the dryads of Shanodin Forest are seen only when they wish to be.
In the Jamuraan jungles, there is often no separating beauty from danger.
Summer sends its kiss with warmth and blooming life.
Moss-covered statues littered the area, a macabre monument to the basilisk's terrible power.
These are its last days. Better to grow broad and heavy. Better that the enemy is crushed beneath its carcass.
"Is it true that the apes wear furs of gold when they marry?" —Rana, Suq'Ata market fool
"To pass through the jungle: silence, courtesy, ferocity, as the occasion demands." —Kamau, "Proper Passage"
Some say magic was first practiced by women, who have always felt strong ties to the land.
"After waking to the magic of Llanowar, no dreams can compare." —Mirri of the *Weatherlight*
The trees have ears, eyes, and teeth.
"Too much work—it takes a long time to break them in, and more than a few recruits." —Grebog, goblin swine-rider
"Aselbo soon had the rhino eating from his palm and the snake waiting at his heels." —Afari, *Tales*
"When one wolf calls, others follow. Who wants to fight creatures that eat scorpions?" —Maimun al-Wyluli, diary
". . . The magician drew a ring off his finger . . . , saying: 'It is a talisman against all evil, so long as you obey me.'" —*The Arabian Nights*, Junior Classics trans.
Tawnos finally cracked the puzzle: the strange structures did not house Mishra's malevolent creations but were themselves among his creations.
The Brothers' War scarred the land, but Ashnod left her mark in the bloodlines of those she tortured.
Pass me from soul to soul, / soldier to herder, herder to beast, beast to soil / until I am everywhere. / Then pass me those souls. —Totem inscription (translated)
Bobbing merrily from opponent to opponent, the scimitar began adding playful little flourishes to its strokes; it even turned a couple of somersaults.
"How is it the legged engines seem so much more alive than their wheeled counterparts? Simply, they were born, not made." —Mishra
"With no further options, I was forced to don the mask." —Rashida Scalebane
The fountain had stood in the town square for centuries, but only the pigeons knew its secret.
Mouths and wings beyond numbering, but a single mind to guide them.
This timeworn relic was responsible for many of Urza's victories, though he never fully comprehended its mystic runes.
Slow and heavy swings the club.
When the mighty sleep, the lowly prowl.
More than one mage has been driven insane by the sound of the millstone relentlessly grinding away.
"The foot stone is connected to the ankle stone, the ankle stone is connected to the leg stone . . . ." —"Song of the Artificer"
"It has been my honor to improve on the Thran's original design. Perhaps history will remember me in some small part for my work." —Urza, in his apprenticeship
It scattered falcons like a lion hunting among jackals.
A mirror, a shield, a promise, a great distance, and a kind word—five ways to avoid harm.
"The secrets of Phyrexia are expensive. You will pay in brass and bone, steel and sinew." —Kaervek
"What manner of fiend would design such a sadistic device?" —Sorine Relicbane, Soldevi heretic
"Uh, does anyone have a flute?" —Rana, Suq'Ata market fool
You'll never miss what you never had.
